physicalNotes: Radius 0.28040016 Jupiter radii from Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 20,046.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0316 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 8.082354 d
sources.shape: Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.080496 au and stellar radius 1.24 solar radii; Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL_2025): inclination derived from its transit duration 3.5635 h and Rp/R* 0.0232 with the orbit's a/R* 13.9591 (Winn 2010, eqs. 14 and 16)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2460298.678071 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 6 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
